function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

import unittest

from app.render import render_message


class RenderMessageTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_layout_contains_recipient_and_body(self):
        out = render_message("Alice Ng", "Your order #A-4471 has shipped.")

        self.assertIn("Sent with NotifyHub", out)

        out = render_message("Bjorn", "Welcome aboard, thanks for joining.")
        self.assertIn("Welcome aboard, thanks for joining.", out)

# NotifyHub

NotifyHub turns queued notifications into the branded messages recipients receive. Every
notification carries a `recipient` (the person's display name) and a `body` (the text the
sender composed). `app/render.py:render_message(recipient, body)` produces the final
message.

## Message layout

Messages are rendered with Jinja2. A fixed layout frames every message:

```
To: {{ recipient }}

{{ body }}

— Sent with NotifyHub
```

## Tests

```
make test
```

The project depends only on Jinja2 and the standard library; the tests need no network or
services.
